task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 27, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about the planned Lantern Shift child care center and the limits of its coverage for families working outside ordinary daytime hours.

facts.text: The Lantern Shift employer consortium announced Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, that its evening child care center is scheduled to open Oct. 12.
The consortium consists of a parcel depot, a food-packing plant and a hotel laundry in East Varn.
The center will have 20 places at any one time for children ages 3 through 10.
Sessions will start at 4 p.m. Monday through Friday and end at 2 a.m. the following morning; no sessions start on Saturday or Sunday.
Fourteen families have reserved regular bookings, but the number present on each evening will depend on their shifts.
Families will pay $5 per child per booked hour; the first-year employer subsidy is intended to cover the remaining budgeted operating costs, not unlimited cost overruns.
The employers have committed a combined $240,000 operating subsidy; the separate $160,000 refit budget has no payer breakdown in the supplied record.
The subsidy commitment expires after one year; future family fees have not been set.
Parents employed by consortium members receive booking priority; other local families may use remaining places.
The center has hired a director and four qualified care workers and is recruiting two relief staff.
A final premises inspection is booked for September, and the opening remains conditional on approval.
Laundry worker Miri Gant said her current arrangement depends on her sister collecting her child when late shifts overrun.
Gant said, "I need to book care for the shift I actually work, not the one printed a month ago."
The consortium will allow booking changes without a fee until noon on the day before care is needed.
Later changes will be charged unless the center fills the place, according to the announced booking policy.
Center director Olla Reed said, "Twenty places are a start, but they are not a solution for every night worker in town."
The three employers together have 1,180 employees, but they have not published the number needing child care.
The center will use rooms in a former community training building, with separate quiet and active areas.
The town previously funded a short evening-care pilot that ended in 2022 when its grant expired.
No retention, absence or productivity results exist for the unopened center.

forbidden_additions: An already approved or operating center, sessions starting on weekends or places for every employee's family
Proven retention or productivity gains before opening
